text:
Tara: Quick RFC-2025 follow-up: I'm worried about silent quality drops when runtime squeezes bitwidths. Proposing a "safety ceiling" mechanism: runtime may lower bitwidth only if an online "quality escrow" pool (shadowed high-precision runs) shows no regression for N requests. Otherwise it must keep current bitwidth. Thoughts?

Ben: Interesting. How big is the escrow pool? We can't shadow every request at fp32/fp16 cost. Maybe sample 1 in 500 or adaptive sampling when risk signal spikes.

Ibrahim: Sampling seems right. Also define a measurable threshold: e.g., if average perplexity_delta over escrow samples > 1.5% revert. Need hysteresis windows to avoid thrash.

Sofia: From product side, add endpoint.quality_mode = escrowed|immediate. escrowed = default, immediate = allow runtime to act without escrow (for aggressive cost customers). Also surface in UI when escrow sampling is active.

Tara: Implementation sketch: runtime tracks candidate_lowering events. When candidate chosen, start escrow sampling for M requests or T seconds. If escrow samples pass, commit and emit event commit_lowering. If fail, emit revert event and blacklist that layer/shape combo for K hours.

Ben: What about privacy on escrow samples? We should default to request_hash+metadata only; payloads encrypted and only used for customer-approved debugging.

Ibrahim: Need ops tooling: `ri quant-escrow --endpoint E --since 6h` to show pending escrow trials, pass/fail counts, and blacklist entries. Also expose an API to force-accept a commit (for customer-approved cost saves).

quant-bot: Quick stat: on a 1k-sample test, escrow sampling prevented 78% of notable regressions when using aggressive lowering. Report: /reports/escrow-quickcheck-2026-03. :robot_face:

Sofia: Nice. Action items:
- Tara: write safety-ceiling section for RFC (due Fri)
- Ben: add adaptive-sampler prototype (end of sprint)
- Ibrahim: add audit CLI and blacklist semantics (PR next Wed)
- Sofia: UI copy for quality_mode and escrow status (mock by Thurs)

Tara: One more edge: if kernel missing and runtime uses shim, escrow should still run but compare shim vs compiled reference to avoid masking shim degradation.

Ben: Good call. We'll ensure escrow always compares to compiled reference when available; otherwise mark sample as "reference_unavailable" and treat conservatively.

Ibrahim: Also record failure reasons with tags: perplexity_delta, degeneracy_rate, last_token_confidence so triage is faster.

Sofia: +1 on everything. No blockers.

Tara: Thanks all :thumbsup:

Ben: +1

Ibrahim: +1

Sofia: +1
